words.meaning: to compare the advantages and disadvantages of a choice
words.japaneseMeaning: 比較してよく検討する
words.example: We need to weigh up the costs and benefits.

words.meaning: to decide that something is not possible or suitable
words.example: We can't rule out a change in the schedule.

sentencePractice.prompt: This option is impossible, so we can ____ that option and consider the others.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: An impossible option is eliminated, not compared further or invented.

words.meaning: to understand or solve something by thinking
words.japaneseMeaning: 理解する・解決法を見つける
words.example: I'm trying to figure out why the printer won't work.

words.meaning: to think of an idea or solution
words.example: Can you come up with a better title?

words.meaning: to consider a fact when making a decision
words.example: We must take into account the needs of part-time staff.

words.meaning: to decide what you want to do
words.example: You don't have to make up your mind today.

words.meaning: to avoid deciding too soon so several choices remain
words.example: I'm applying to several colleges to keep my options open.

words.meaning: after considering both the good and bad points
words.example: On balance, the new timetable works better.

words.meaning: over a long period rather than immediately
words.example: Better insulation saves money in the long run.

words.meaning: a choice in which gaining one benefit means losing another
words.japaneseMeaning: 何かを得るために別の利点を失うこと
words.example: There is a trade-off between cost and speed.
